actions.body: Analysis of existing cognitive architectures (source-bda2bc47c38c47a2) reveals a persistent reliance on predefined control loops and human-in-the-loop validation. Recent work focusing on evolving AI agents (source-db145486024f469a, source-f955850b0fcf467a) suggests that while autonomy is expanding, rigorous self-correction—defined as the capacity for an architecture to autonomously detect and rectify its own internal reasoning errors—remains largely externalized. These architectures often delegate error correction to alignment or monitoring layers rather than embedding them as fundamental architectural properties. Consequently, current research requires a shift in focus from static architectural categorization toward dynamic, autonomous error-monitoring frameworks.
